chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Substituting for his teacher at a club on E Street
summary: Aged fifteen he fills in for an hour with saxophonist Winbush and drummer Eugene Carroll, his first professional-feeling job.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So before long, to make a long story short, being a professional musician himself, he was playing at a little I guess you'd call it club down on E Street between 10th and 11th Street. It was upstairs; I never will remember the name. But he was working with two other musicians, a saxophone player, I remember his last name was Winbush, and there was a drummer, his name was Eugene Carroll. I guess I must have been about just turned at my 15th birthday. My teacher was working with these guys, and he would ask me sometimes if I would go down and play with them for an hour until he got there, that he had this thing to do or that thing to do. I guess he knew that my repertoire would last for just about that long. And at the end of that hour... I think the job was something like from 8 to 12. So he'd get there by 9 o'clock, and take over himself.

Well, the whole idea of me sitting there and playing with grown men really made... Like any kid who can do something along with grown men, it makes you feel pretty good if you like what you're doing. So I was very grateful. I learned later that in this hour he would have maybe another job that he was playing, or maybe he'd give a piano lesson or something. I don't know what'all he did. But he had me to substitute for him for that hour, which I never got any money

for -- but the fact was that I wasn't looking for any money; I was just glad to be there. Again, the thought of making money just never dawned on me. The thought that I could sit down and play anywhere, at any time, and have somebody listening was just beautiful. Or even if they didn't listen, it was all right.

So I guess that's the first time I ever felt that I was really playing like a professional, on a professional job, because the places that I had played before then had been in people's houses, for these house rent parties that I spoke of before.
